items.question: An operations manager is designing a three-stage prompt chain: (1) extract data from 50 reports; (2) analyse patterns across the extracted data; (3) draft an executive briefing. Which TWO design decisions would MOST improve chain reliability? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Include the full output of each stage explicitly in the input to the next stage, labelled as the source data for that step.
options.B: Run all three stages in parallel to reduce total processing time.
options.C: Use the same prompt template for all three stages to maintain structural consistency.
options.D: Require each stage to end with a completion marker — such as "EXTRACTION COMPLETE: 50 records" — so truncation is detectable before the next stage begins.
options.E: Assign each stage to a different model tier based on the complexity of that stage's task.

items.question: A content team lead is auditing their Claude Project's instruction set before the quarterly review. Which TWO signs indicate the instruction set needs consolidation? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The project has been active for more than 6 months.
options.B: Two instructions in the set give Claude conflicting guidance about output length for the same task type.
options.C: The instruction set has grown to 50 items covering overlapping areas, added incrementally by multiple team members without a review process.
options.D: The project knowledge base contains documents uploaded more than 3 months ago.
options.E: The project is shared across more than 10 team members.

items.question: What term describes any information that can identify a living individual directly or indirectly?

options.A: Protected Health Information
options.B: Payment Card Industry data
options.C: Personally Identifiable Information
options.D: Privileged and Confidential data

items.question: Which data category links an individual's identity to their health status, medical treatment, or healthcare payment?

options.A: Protected Health Information
options.B: Personally Identifiable Information
options.C: Payment Card Industry data
options.D: Biometric data

items.question: Which privacy principle requires limiting data collection to only what is necessary for a stated purpose?

options.A: Least privilege
options.B: Data minimisation
options.C: Purpose limitation
options.D: Data residency

items.question: What makes PHI a stricter regulatory category than general PII?

options.A: PHI cannot be stored digitally under any privacy framework.
options.B: PHI always requires explicit written consent, while PII requires only a privacy notice.
options.C: PHI applies exclusively to government-held health records.
options.D: PHI combines personal identity with health, treatment, or payment-for-care information, triggering healthcare-specific obligations beyond standard PII rules.

items.question: Which control removes or masks sensitive identifiers from a document before it is submitted to an AI model?

options.A: Redaction
options.B: Pseudonymisation
options.C: Tokenisation
options.D: Encryption

items.question: What governance principle prohibits using personal data collected for one purpose to serve a materially different purpose?

options.A: Data minimisation
options.B: Least privilege
options.C: Purpose limitation
options.D: Data residency

items.question: Which term specifically covers credit card numbers, CVV codes, and payment account details under payment security frameworks?

options.A: PHI
options.B: PCI-scoped data
options.C: Commercially confidential information
options.D: Quasi-identifiers

items.question: Data minimisation and least privilege are both data-protection controls. What is the correct distinction between them?

options.A: Data minimisation applies to stored data; least privilege applies only to data in transit.
options.B: Least privilege is a technical control; data minimisation is a legal principle with no technical implementation.
options.C: Both restrict access to data, but data minimisation is enforced at the network layer while least privilege is enforced at the application layer.
options.D: Data minimisation governs what data is collected or retained; least privilege governs who is permitted to access data that has already been collected.

items.question: Which TWO of the following actions constitute data minimisation when preparing input for an AI tool? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Removing dataset fields that are not relevant to the analytical task
options.B: Encrypting the dataset before uploading it to an enterprise AI platform
options.C: Replacing full names with anonymised role identifiers such as 'Employee A'
options.D: Storing the AI-generated output in an access-controlled repository
options.E: Using a higher-tier model to process a smaller number of requests per day

items.question: What is the key difference between anonymisation and pseudonymisation as data de-identification techniques?

options.A: Anonymisation is irreversible and prevents re-identification; pseudonymisation replaces identifiers with a reversible token that can be re-linked to the original.
options.B: Anonymisation is suited to real-time processing; pseudonymisation requires batch pipelines.
options.C: Pseudonymisation removes all identifying fields; anonymisation replaces them with fictional values.
options.D: Anonymisation applies only to digital records; pseudonymisation applies to both digital and physical records.

items.question: What is the primary data-governance risk of submitting commercially sensitive client information to a consumer-grade AI tool?

options.A: The AI may produce lower-quality outputs when processing complex commercial content.
options.B: Consumer tools lack formatting features required for professional documents.
options.C: Response latency is typically too high for time-sensitive client work.
options.D: Client data may be used to train the AI model or otherwise leave the organisation's control.

items.question: Which of the following is a PII element that is NOT classified as PHI when held by a retailer with no healthcare connection?

options.A: A patient's hospital admission date
options.B: A customer's home mailing address in a retail loyalty programme
options.C: A prescription drug name linked to a named patient
options.D: A health insurer's record of a member's diagnosis code

items.question: What is the primary purpose of a data processing agreement between an organisation and an AI vendor?

options.A: To cap the monthly cost of API usage under a fixed contract rate
options.B: To restrict the AI vendor from competing with the organisation's products
options.C: To define the lawful basis and obligations for processing personal data on the organisation's behalf
options.D: To guarantee a minimum service-level uptime for the AI platform

items.question: Which TWO data types are typically classified as special-category sensitive data requiring heightened protection beyond standard PII under major privacy frameworks? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Employee job titles
options.B: Biometric data processed to uniquely identify an individual
options.C: Business email addresses
options.D: Home postal codes
options.E: Data revealing racial or ethnic origin

items.question: What does cross-border data transfer governance primarily regulate?

options.A: The movement of personal data to jurisdictions with different or weaker legal protections
options.B: The bandwidth used when uploading large datasets to cloud services
options.C: The number of staff permitted to access data held in foreign data centres
options.D: The encryption format required when transmitting personal data internationally

items.question: What distinguishes a data controller from a data processor under major privacy frameworks?

options.A: A controller processes data; a processor only stores it.
options.B: A controller must be a public authority; a processor can be any type of organisation.
options.C: A controller is always the organisation that collected the data directly from the individual.
options.D: A controller determines the purpose and means of processing; a processor processes data on the controller's instructions.

items.question: What term describes a data element that does not identify an individual on its own but can do so when combined with other available information?

options.A: Sensitive personal data
options.B: Anonymised data
options.C: Quasi-identifier
options.D: Pseudonymous data

items.question: Which privacy principle specifically prohibits retaining personal data beyond the period necessary for its original purpose?

options.A: Data minimisation
options.B: Storage limitation
options.C: Least privilege
options.D: Purpose limitation

items.question: Which TWO steps should be completed before submitting a document containing personal data to a shared AI tool? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Redact or mask personal identifiers that are not required for the task
options.B: Increase the document's font size to improve AI readability
options.C: Convert the document to a compressed archive format
options.D: Confirm the tool's data retention and model training policies
options.E: Split the document into equal-length segments before uploading

items.question: Which THREE of the following are typically classed as special-category data under major privacy frameworks? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Health and medical data
options.B: Residential postal addresses
options.C: Biometric data processed for unique identification
options.D: Full name combined with date of birth
options.E: Data revealing religious or philosophical beliefs

items.question: What is the purpose of disclosing AI involvement in a high-stakes decision to the affected individual?

options.A: To obtain the individual's permission before the decision is made
options.B: To inform the individual that AI contributed to the process so they can seek clarification or challenge the outcome
options.C: To satisfy a record-keeping obligation that applies only to public-sector organisations
options.D: To enable the individual to opt out of future AI-assisted decisions across all platforms

items.question: What is a prompt injection attack?

options.A: A technique for improving model output by embedding structured examples in the system prompt
options.B: A method of compressing large documents before submitting them to an AI model
options.C: An attempt to bypass model safety constraints through the user's own direct instructions
options.D: Malicious instructions embedded in untrusted external content that redirect an AI model's behaviour

items.question: What is shadow AI in an organisational context?

options.A: Use of AI tools by employees outside the knowledge or approval of the organisation's IT or governance function
options.B: The unintentional drift in an AI model's behaviour due to insufficient context across sessions
options.C: A hidden AI capability that activates only when specific trigger phrases appear in a prompt
options.D: An AI system that operates without a user interface, processing data automatically in the background

items.question: What is the distinction between disclosure and consent in the context of AI-assisted decision-making?

options.A: Disclosure is required only for fully automated decisions; consent applies only to human-assisted decisions.
options.B: Consent and disclosure are legally equivalent terms used interchangeably in most privacy frameworks.
options.C: Disclosure informs an individual that AI was involved in the process; consent obtains the individual's agreement before the AI involvement proceeds.
options.D: Disclosure is an internal record-keeping obligation; consent is an external communication requirement.

items.question: What is the key functional difference between an audit trail and an access control list?

options.A: An audit trail records who performed which actions and when; an access control list specifies who is permitted to perform which actions.
options.B: An access control list is updated after each user action; an audit trail defines permissions before access is granted.
options.C: An audit trail prevents unauthorised access in real time; an access control list documents actions after they occur.
options.D: Both serve identical governance purposes but are implemented in different technical environments.

items.question: What distinguishes a prompt injection attack from a jailbreak attempt?

options.A: Prompt injection targets the model's system prompt; jailbreak targets the human turn of the conversation.
options.B: Jailbreak attacks require technical API access; prompt injection can be performed without any technical knowledge.
options.C: Prompt injection and jailbreak are different vendor names for the same underlying attack pattern.
options.D: Prompt injection embeds adversarial instructions in untrusted content processed by the model; a jailbreak is when the user's own input attempts to override the model's safety constraints.

items.question: Which categories of decisions are generally considered to require a human decision-maker and cannot safely be delegated to an AI alone?

options.A: Routine data entry, invoice matching, and document formatting tasks
options.B: Hiring, credit and lending, clinical, disciplinary, and legally consequential determinations
options.C: Any decision that references a database or structured dataset
options.D: Decisions made more than once per day due to the volume and speed involved

items.question: What does the accountability principle require when AI contributes to a consequential decision?

options.A: The AI vendor is legally responsible for any incorrect decision the model helped produce.
options.B: The decision must be reversed if the AI model's confidence score falls below a defined threshold.
options.C: A named human or organisation must remain identifiable as responsible for the outcome and capable of explaining it.
options.D: All AI-assisted decisions must be pre-approved by a dedicated AI ethics committee before being communicated.

items.question: Which TWO of the following are organisational governance controls over employee AI tool use? (Choose TWO)

options.A: An acceptable-use policy defining approved tools, permitted data types, and required review steps
options.B: Upgrading to a higher-tier AI model to reduce the risk of incorrect outputs
options.C: Adjusting the temperature parameter to produce more consistent AI outputs
options.D: Role-based access controls that restrict which staff may access certain AI capabilities or Projects
options.E: Increasing prompt specificity to reduce the frequency of off-topic responses

items.question: What is the distinction between bias in an AI model's output and unfairness in an AI-assisted decision?

options.A: Bias is a statistical property; unfairness occurs only when a human intentionally acts on biased output.
options.B: Unfairness is introduced by training data; bias is introduced by the prompting strategy.
options.C: Bias describes a systematic skew in model outputs; unfairness occurs when a decision process produces discriminatory outcomes for protected groups, which bias can cause but is not identical to.
options.D: Bias and unfairness are legally synonymous terms used interchangeably in all major AI governance frameworks.

items.question: What does consent require that disclosure alone does not, when an organisation uses AI in a process affecting an individual?

options.A: Consent requires the organisation to publish the decision in an auditable log; disclosure does not.
options.B: Consent requires the individual's active agreement before the process proceeds; disclosure only requires informing them, potentially after the fact.
options.C: Consent applies only in healthcare contexts; disclosure applies universally across all sectors.
options.D: Disclosure is a one-time obligation that never requires renewal; consent must be renewed annually.

items.question: What is the primary governance purpose of role-based access control in a shared AI platform?

options.A: To ensure each user accesses only the data and capabilities appropriate to their role, limiting exposure if credentials are compromised or misused.
options.B: To prevent the AI model from generating outputs that exceed the user's professional expertise level.
options.C: To restrict the AI model's training on data produced by specific roles within the organisation.
options.D: To log all user interactions with the AI platform for compliance reporting.

items.question: What governance function does an audit trail serve in an AI-assisted workflow?

options.A: It prevents users from submitting non-compliant prompts by blocking them before submission.
options.B: It restricts user access to AI tools based on the user's security clearance level.
options.C: It automatically corrects AI outputs that deviate from approved templates or policies.
options.D: It creates a timestamped record of who performed which actions, enabling post-hoc review and accountability.

items.question: Why is AI-generated legal, medical, or financial advice subject to acceptable-use limits?

options.A: AI models lack the language capability to address legal or medical topics with adequate fluency.
options.B: Legal and medical content is blocked by default in all enterprise AI platforms.
options.C: Consequential professional advice requires accountability, contextual judgement, and regulatory oversight that only a qualified human professional can provide.
options.D: AI models cannot access current legislation or medical guidelines without live internet connectivity.

items.question: Which TWO characteristics most clearly make a decision 'high-stakes' in the AI governance sense? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The decision is made by a senior employee rather than a junior one.
options.B: The outcome materially affects an individual's rights, livelihood, health, or freedom.
options.C: The decision requires querying more than two internal databases.
options.D: The AI model is invoked more than once in the same workflow.
options.E: The decision is difficult or costly to reverse once communicated.

items.question: What is the primary organisational risk created by employees using unapproved AI tools?

options.A: Sensitive data submitted to unapproved tools operates outside the organisation's data-handling agreements and governance controls.
options.B: Unapproved AI tools typically produce lower-quality outputs that damage the organisation's client reputation.
options.C: Shadow AI increases cloud infrastructure costs because unapproved tools bypass the organisation's volume pricing agreements.
options.D: Employees using unapproved tools receive outputs that cannot be reviewed or corrected by a supervisor.

items.question: Which access control design prevents a customer support agent from accessing patient health data stored in the same AI platform as a clinical team?

options.A: Multi-factor authentication requiring an extra login step for the clinical module
options.B: End-to-end encryption of all data in transit between users and the AI platform
options.C: A prompt-level instruction telling the AI not to discuss patient health information with support agents
options.D: Role-based access control restricting each role to only the Projects and data categories relevant to their function

items.question: What is the key difference between third-party AI vendor risk and shadow AI risk in an organisation?

options.A: Third-party vendor risk is primarily financial; shadow AI risk is primarily reputational.
options.B: Third-party vendor risk arises from approved tools with governance gaps; shadow AI risk arises from unapproved tools operating entirely outside governance.
options.C: Shadow AI risk affects only large enterprises; third-party vendor risk affects organisations of all sizes equally.
options.D: Third-party vendors are subject to regulation; shadow AI tools are exempt from all legal obligations.

items.question: Which TWO practices reflect correct acceptable-use limits when using AI for legal or medical content? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A qualified professional reviews and takes ownership of any AI-drafted legal document before it is finalised.
options.B: AI-generated medical summaries are delivered directly to patients without review when the model's stated confidence is high.
options.C: AI assists with research and drafting, but the final advice or clinical decision is made by a licensed professional.
options.D: AI-generated legal clauses are inserted into contracts automatically once the model rates them above a quality threshold.
options.E: Medical AI outputs replace specialist consultation when scheduling constraints make consultation impractical.

items.question: Which TWO conditions must be satisfied for accountability to be fulfilled in an AI-assisted consequential decision? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The AI model must be able to provide a natural-language explanation of its own reasoning.
options.B: A named human or organisational role must be identifiable as responsible for the decision outcome.
options.C: The AI tool used must carry third-party certification from an accredited testing authority.
options.D: The responsible party must be capable of explaining and defending the decision, including the AI's contribution to it.
options.E: The decision must be logged in a compliance audit trail within 24 hours of being made.

items.question: What is the primary copyright concern with using AI-generated text in a commercial product?

options.A: AI-generated text is always in the public domain and may be used freely without restriction.
options.B: The model developer automatically holds copyright over all text the model produces.
options.C: AI-generated text may lack copyright protection because it was not created by a human author, leaving the product's IP position weaker than expected.
options.D: Copyright in AI-generated text always vests in the user who wrote the prompt.

items.question: What is the first governance obligation when AI-generated output causes demonstrable harm to an identified individual?

options.A: Contain the harm by halting or correcting the erroneous output and preserving evidence for investigation.
options.B: Conduct a full root-cause analysis of the AI model's training data before taking any other action.
options.C: Escalate immediately to the AI vendor so they can issue a patch to the model.
options.D: Publish a public transparency statement disclosing the AI's role within 24 hours.

items.question: What is the primary function of an acceptable-use policy for AI tools within an organisation?

options.A: To specify the prompting techniques employees must use to maximise output quality.
options.B: To define which tools are approved, what data may be submitted, and what review obligations apply before outputs are used.
options.C: To negotiate commercial pricing with AI vendors on behalf of the organisation.
options.D: To specify the technical security architecture required for deploying AI tools.

items.question: Who typically holds IP rights in a document produced solely by an AI model under current frameworks?

options.A: The AI model developer, because the model performed the creative work.
options.B: The organisation whose server hosted the AI model at the time of generation.
options.C: The user, because writing the prompt constitutes sufficient creative authorship in most jurisdictions.
options.D: The document may attract no copyright protection in many jurisdictions because copyright typically requires a human author.

items.question: Which architectural control MOST effectively reduces prompt injection risk when an AI tool processes untrusted documents?

options.A: Applying strict structural boundaries in the prompt that separate the AI's instructions from the document content, treating document text as data rather than as commands.
options.B: Requiring users to manually summarise documents before submitting them to the AI.
options.C: Increasing system prompt length to leave less room for injected instructions in the context window.
options.D: Using a lower-tier model that is less capable of following complex injected instructions.

items.question: Which scenario represents AI content that exceeds acceptable-use limits in a medical context?

options.A: A nurse uses AI to draft a structured clinical note that a doctor reviews and co-signs before it enters the patient record.
options.B: A hospital uses AI to summarise a patient's discharge summary for the receiving general practitioner.
options.C: An AI chatbot tells a patient which medication to take and at what dose without any clinical oversight.
options.D: A researcher uses AI to summarise published trial results for a literature review.

items.question: What is the MOST important governance check when procuring an AI tool that will process employee personal data?

options.A: Confirming that the tool offers a higher-tier model option for handling complex analytical tasks.
options.B: Verifying that the vendor will sign a data processing agreement that prohibits training on submitted employee data.
options.C: Ensuring the tool's user interface is accessible and intuitive for non-technical staff.
options.D: Confirming that the vendor's service agreement includes a response-latency performance guarantee.

items.question: What is a hallucination in the context of a large language model output?

options.A: A confident, fluent claim that is factually false and not traceable to any real source
options.B: Output that directly contradicts a statement the user made earlier in the same conversation
options.C: A model's refusal to answer a question it cannot verify from context
options.D: A tendency to agree with the user's position when challenged on a prior response
